title: Uniqueness from low-degree Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued functions. Suppose $f$ is represented as the threshold sign of a multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$, with zero assigned sign $1$, and suppose $f$ and $g$ have equal Fourier–Walsh coefficients at every subset of coordinates of cardinality at most $k$. Then $g=f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a polynomial threshold function of degree at most $k$
The Fourier–Walsh coefficients of $f$ and $g$ agree for every coordinate subset of size at most $k$
replaced:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E_x[h(x)\chi_S(x)]$ using uniform expectation, for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$.
Suppose $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$ for a real multilinear polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{|S|\le k}a_S\chi_S(x)$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
If $\widehat g(S)=\widehat f(S)$ for every $S$ with $|S|\le k$, then $g=f$.
